Ben —

Our contract hits renewal in late July and usage has grown faster than forecast. We99re evaluating a move to a premium SLA and want to understand Redwood99s options for:

- Committing to a 24-month term in exchange for a discounted rate
- Adding a latency SLO for our core inference path (p95 target + credit policy)
- Reserving dedicated capacity for daytime peaks (US primary, 8am-8pm PT) with burst allowance

Attached is our Q2 usage export so you can see hourly load. High-level asks from Atlas: a clear SLO with remediation credits, one-page addendum that legal can sign, and a simple path to ramp capacity during Q4.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call next week to get alignment? Priyanka

psingh@atlashealth.com

Forwarding Priyanka99s note — Atlas is asking for a premium SLA addendum and capacity reservation. Quick summary of what I think we should propose:

- 24-month committed term with a 12% committed usage discount
- Premium SLA: availability + latency band (p95 target for our inference API) with a credit schedule (tiered credits for p95 misses)
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) sized for average daytime + 20% burst; hosted fallback to avoid hard outages
- One-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 1 month of commitment)

I99ve attached a draft SLA we can iterate on. Need Aditya to confirm the latency numbers are feasible for their traffic profile and Marissa to own the onboarding + support uplift offering. Can everyone take a look and drop notes by EOD Friday? I99ll propose meeting times once we have internal alignment.

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_SLA_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Ben
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract renewal + premium SLA inquiry

Thanks Ben — quick thoughts after skimming Priyanka99s usage file:

- Recommend offering two SLO options to keep negotiations simple:
  1) Premium SLO A: p95 <= 200ms (US) with 99.90% monthly availability and small credits for single-event breaches.
  2) Premium SLO B: p95 <= 250ms with larger credits but lower committed cost.
- Suggest dedicated capacity for daytime peak with an automated hosted-fallback route. That lets Atlas keep latency guarantees while we preserve availability if they spike beyond reserved pool.
- Ask engineering (Aditya) to validate p95 curves at 512-token avg and at 1.5x concurrency expected in Q4.
- From commercial: propose a 24-month term with a 10% uplift commitment discount and a 1-month onboarding credit.

Action items:
- Aditya: validate latency feasibility and estimate cost delta (dedicated vs hosted fallback).
- Marissa: draft a support uplift package (SLAs, priority oncall, escalation playbook) and a customer onboarding timeline.
- Ben: coordinate the 30-min call with Atlas and prep a one-pager for legal.

Availability for a sync: Thu 06/19 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 06/20 13:00-15:00 PT.

Sofia
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract renewal + premium SLA inquiry

Quick technical readout from infra:

- Baseline: for their median request size (approx 350 tokens) on a dedicated A100 fleet we see p95 around 140-180ms under steady-state single-tenant load.
- At 1.5x concurrency and short bursts we expect the p95 to drift toward ~200-230ms unless we tune batching/caching aggressively.
- Recommendation: offer SLO A at p95 <= 200ms but include a requirement for a small token-prefetch/k-v cache (we can provide a configuration recipe). For heavier bursts, rely on hosted fallback; credits kick in only if both dedicated and fallback fail to meet SLO.
- I'll attach the latency calc workbook and include rough cost delta estimates for a +25% reserved pool.

We can meet the numbers but need to be explicit about assumptions in the addendum (typical seq length, concurrency profile, region).

Attachment: latency_calc.xlsx

- Aditya
